summary: Adversarial pass over SCHED-6 (autonomous jobs pause-and-ask on tool denial). Five findings; four resolved in the plan, one parked as an explicit non-goal.
gaps: The denied-tool terminal failure could enter the normal retry/backoff path and dead-letter a job that merely needs approval, burning attempts while it waits.

An under-declared grantable denial has no stored access_requirements entry to map, so the SCHED-4B card would fall to instruction-only unless a requirement is synthesized — the one-tap-approve behavior needs the requirement created.
Making the deny terminal is broad; a legitimate autonomous flow that relied on soft-deny-and-continue would break silently.
contradictions: One-tap approve that ADDS a tool to the job's access_requirements looks like a scheduled run mutating its own job, which 0106 forbids.
Requirement 6 (protocol unchanged) vs the fear that terminal-on-denial requires touching the zero-timeout synchronous permission protocol.
resolutions: Pinned as criterion 4a + a stated invariant: a denied-tool terminal failure routes to the setup-pause (awaiting-approval) state and must NOT consume a retry/backoff attempt or dead-letter; Codex D2/D4 shows finalization already routes denied-tool -> setup-pause; a verify check asserts the retry budget is untouched.

SCHED-6-2 explicitly synthesizes the grantable requirement from the denied tool identity and, on the single Allow-for-future approval, both adds it to the job's access_requirements and grants it to the agent via the existing persistRequestPermissionRules + recheck chain.

Codex D4 verified no documented soft-deny-continue flow exists; the only dependents are two tests asserting non-pausing, deliberately updated; the verify step re-runs the full jobs+runner suites as the blast-radius net.

Contradiction resolved: the add-to-requirements is HUMAN-initiated (the approver acting on the card), not the autonomous run self-mutating, so it stays within 0106; called out in the approach and criterion 2.

Contradiction resolved: Codex D6 confirms flipping denyNonPromptableAutonomousRecovery to interrupt:true + terminal telemetry follows the existing terminal diagnostic path and does NOT touch the synchronous zero-timeout protocol.
open_items: Full 'no autonomous guard ever soft-denies' sweep of the pre-autonomous guards (protected-capability, memory-boundary, model-validation, wait-only, network) is deliberately OUT of SCHED-6 scope and parked as a follow-up; SCHED-6 targets only the confirmed silent-degradation seam.
